subtopics.title: Solving Like an Equation — With One Exception

questions.question: The inequality sign must be reversed when you:
options: Add a negative number to both sides
Multiply or divide both sides by a negative number
Subtract the same number from both sides
Divide both sides by a positive number

questions.question: Solve 3x − 5 ≤ 7.
Solve −2x > 6.
Why does multiplying by a negative reverse the order of two numbers?
options: Because negative numbers cannot be compared
Because zero is neither positive nor negative
Because it reflects both numbers through zero, and reflection reverses their order — 5 > 3 but −5 < −3

subtopics.title: The Number Line and Interval Notation

questions.question: A solid, filled dot on a number line means:
options: The boundary value is included — the sign has a bar (≤ or ≥)
The shading runs to the right

questions.question: In interval notation, infinity always takes:
options: A round bracket, because infinity can never be reached
Whichever bracket the other end has

questions.question: x ≤ 4 written in interval notation is:
If a question states that x is an integer, the number-line answer becomes:
options: A continuous shaded arrow as usual
A set of separate dots rather than continuous shading

subtopics.title: Compound Inequalities — Trapped Between Two Fences

questions.question: Solve −3 < 2x + 1 ≤ 7.
In a compound inequality, every operation must be applied to:
The number-line picture of −2 < x ≤ 3 is:
options: Two arrows pointing outwards from −2 and 3
Solid dots at both ends with shading between
An open dot at −2, a solid dot at 3, and shading only between them
A solid dot at −2, an open dot at 3, with an arrow to the right

questions.question: Dividing a compound inequality by a negative number requires that:
options: BOTH signs reverse and the statement is rewritten with the smaller value on the left

subtopics.title: Word Problems, Integers, and the Trap Museum

questions.question: The Mthatha stallholder pays R120 for her table and sells vetkoek at R12 each. For a profit of at least R300, the inequality is:
Solving it gives:
Which phrase means 'less than or equal to'?
In a context question, an answer left as 'n ≥ 35' with nothing further loses a mark because:
options: 35 should be rejected as a boundary
The examiner wants the interpretation in the language of the problem — at least 35 vetkoek

questions.question: R500 is more than R300, but owing R500 is worse than owing R300. This shows that:
options: Negative numbers are always smaller than positive ones
−500 < −300 — turning amounts into debts flips the comparison

questions.question: Which operation leaves the heavier side heavier?
Substituting x = 0 into −2x > 6 gives 0 > 6, which is false. This proves that:
options: The original inequality has no solution
The unflipped answer x > −3 must be wrong

questions.question: The recommended way to be certain about a flip is to:
options: Memorise the rule and move on
Always write the answer with x on the right
Test one value from your answer in the ORIGINAL inequality

questions.question: 'Eighteen and over' versus 'over eighteen' illustrates:
options: The difference between a filled dot (boundary included) and a hollow dot (boundary excluded)
The need to flip the sign
Why infinity gets a round bracket
Why compound inequalities have three parts

questions.question: A square bracket in interval notation corresponds to:
options: A filled dot — the number is invited

questions.question: Intervals must always be written:
options: With the smaller number first, left to right as on the number line
Using square brackets on both ends

subtopics.title: Between Two Fences, and the Vetkoek Test

questions.question: A salary 'more than R8 000 but at most R12 000' is drawn as:
options: A filled dot at R8 000 and a hollow dot at R12 000
A hollow dot at R8 000 and a filled dot at R12 000, shaded between

questions.question: Selling exactly 35 vetkoek gives income R420, less the R120 table, which is:
options: Exactly R300 profit — so 35 counts and its dot is filled in

questions.question: Solving a compound inequality by 'doing the same thing to all three parts' on −3 < 2x + 1 ≤ 7 begins with:
Which pair of phrases EXCLUDES the boundary value?
options: No less than; no more than
